title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes, the continuation of La Longue Marche. There Grothendieck studies the profinite Teichmüller tower in genus 0 and genus 1 and the automorphism groups acting on it.

- rho and sigma are the torsion elements of orders 6 and 4. These are the standard generators of SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, viewed inside an automorphism group of the profinite fundamental group.
- Pi_0 (completed: hat-Pi_0) is a normal subgroup, presumably the profinite fundamental group of the once-punctured elliptic curve, a free profinite group of rank 2.
- M^![0] = Z^!_{rho,sigma} is a group of automorphisms u.
- epsilon_3(u) = ±1 is a sign character.
- S_0Gamma^!_{rho,sigma} is a fibre product M^![0] x N^!_rho x N^!_sigma over Gamma_{rho,sigma}, an index-2 subgroup of S_0Gamma_{rho,sigma}. N_rho and N_sigma are normalizers of the cyclic subgroups generated by rho and sigma.

Previous page. Proposition (50) describes the fibre over a fixed u. To u, via (38), are attached alpha and beta, which (from the proof here) lie in Pi_0, with u(sigma) = int(beta)(sigma) and u(rho) = int(alpha)(rho). The triples over u are then exactly a = f'^{-1}u and b = f^{-1}u, where:
- f = beta·sigma^i, with i in Z/4;
- f'·epsilon_3(tau') = alpha·rho^j, with j in Z/6;
- epsilon_3(tau') means 1 or tau' according to the sign epsilon_3.
So the fibre is a torsor under (Z/4) x (Z/6), i.e. 24 lifts.

This page.
- Choosing i = j = 0 gives the 'simplest' lift (51): a = epsilon_3(tau')·alpha^{-1}·u and b = beta^{-1}·u. This is a set-theoretic section of S_0Gamma^! -> Z^!.
- Grothendieck asks whether this section is multiplicative, i.e. whether u ↦ (a,b) is a group homomorphism splitting the extension.

Criterion (Proposition, (52)). A triple (u,a,b) in S_0Gamma^! lies on this section iff u ≡ b ≡ epsilon_3(sigma)·a mod hat-Pi_0, where epsilon_3(sigma) = 1 or sigma according to the sign. This uses the relations tau'·tau = sigma^{-1} and tau'·sigma^{-1} = tau.
- Necessity: beta = u·b^{-1} and epsilon_3(tau) = u·a^{-1}·epsilon_3(sigma^{-1}) lie in Pi_0.
- Sufficiency: (52) says f and f'·epsilon_3(sigma^{-1}) lie in Pi_0. Reduce in the quotient group (Aut-type group)/Pi_0 using alpha·dot = beta·dot = 1 and epsilon_3(tau)·dot·alpha·dot = 1. This gives sigma·dot^i = 1 and rho·dot^j = 1. Since rho and sigma keep their exact orders 6 and 4 modulo Pi_0, this forces i = 0 and j = 0. QED.

Crossed-out corollary. A corollary 'la section ensembliste est multiplicative' was written and then struck out. The next page shows why: multiplicativity reduces to the congruence condition (54), sigma(a') ≡ ±a' mod hat-Pi_0. That condition is non-trivial when epsilon_3 = -1.

What the page serves. It is a step in trying to split, or to compute the obstruction to splitting, the extension of the genus-1 'Teichmüller' automorphism group by the finite (Z/4 x Z/6)-type ambiguity coming from the elliptic torsion points rho, sigma. This is part of Grothendieck's analysis of a GT-like group via the modular group / M_{1,1} level of the tower.
errors: In the sufficiency argument the reduced relation for beta is written as beta·dot·rho·dot^i = 1. By (50) (f = beta·sigma^i) it should read beta·dot·sigma·dot^i = 1; this is a slip of letters.
The concluding line 'rho·dot^i = rho·dot^j = 1' should be 'sigma·dot^i = rho·dot^j = 1'.

Gap: the step from sigma·dot^i = rho·dot^j = 1 to i = j = 0 tacitly assumes that sigma and rho keep orders 4 and 6 in the quotient mod Pi_0, i.e. their cyclic groups meet Pi_0 trivially. This is true in the intended setting (torsion of SL2-type quotient, Pi_0 torsion-free), but it is not stated.

In the necessity step the margin writes epsilon_3(tau) = u·a^{-1}·epsilon_3(tau') = u·a^{-1}·epsilon_3(sigma^{-1}). The second equality requires the NB relations, and the notation tau versus tau' fluctuates. It is consistent only modulo Pi_0, which is all that is used.
The corollary that the section is multiplicative was rightly struck out: the next page shows it holds only under the extra condition (54).

ideas.what: Fibre of S_0Gamma^! over u is a torsor under Z/4 x Z/6 (choices i, j); choice of the canonical lift i = j = 0
ideas.modern_name: set-theoretic section of a group extension by the stabilizers of the elliptic points of orders 4 and 6 in SL2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; the context is the GT / Teichmüller-tower work of Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: the genus-1 discussion of Esquisse d'un programme is only programmatic

ideas.what: Characterization of the lifts lying on the canonical section by congruences mod hat-Pi_0 (52)
ideas.modern_name: congruence criterion for a normalized lift (analogous to normalization conditions on (lambda, f) in GT-hat)

ideas.what: Question whether the canonical section is a homomorphism (splitting), answered on the next page by a sign/congruence obstruction
ideas.modern_name: splitting obstruction of an extension; cocycle given by the sign epsilon

missed.claim: This is a technical step in Grothendieck's unpublished genus-1 analysis of automorphisms of the profinite modular/Teichmüller tower. It normalizes lifts at the elliptic points of orders 4 and 6 (sigma, rho), and he finds that the naive normalized section is not multiplicative. The page itself contains no result beyond routine group theory, but it documents his approach.
missed.quote: je me demande si cette section ensembliste ... est multiplicative
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of interest mainly for comparison with the genus-1 GT literature (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Enriquez's elliptic GT). It records how Grothendieck handled the torsion elements of SL2(Z) when normalizing automorphisms.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine computation, a congruence criterion for a normalized lift, inside a large unpublished framework. The only mildly notable point is that it documents Grothendieck's own handling of the orders-4/6 elliptic points and a splitting obstruction in the genus-1 tower.
transcription_corrections: 's Gamma^!_{j,sigma}' should read 'S_0 Gamma^!_{rho,sigma}' (or 'sGamma^!_{rho,sigma}'); 'j' is a misreading of rho.
In the margin of the demonstration, epsilon_3(tau) = u·a^{-1}·epsilon_3(tau') = u·a^{-1}·epsilon_3(sigma^{-1}); the first symbol is partly crossed.
The line read as 'beta·dot·rho·dot^i = 1' is written that way in the image (apparently), but mathematically it should be beta·dot·sigma·dot^i = 1.
'Démonstration. Comme beta' is followed by an inserted '= ub^{-1}'.
The header number '597' is Grothendieck's own pagination; '586' is the archive page.
